title: The Urantia Book
author: Anonymous (authorship attributed to a group of celestial beings)
edition_analyzed: First Edition (Urantia Foundation, 1955); text remains unchanged in subsequent printings
target_audience: Spiritual seekers and readers of metaphysical literature
Students and scholars of comparative religion and philosophy
Individuals interested in alternative spiritual texts
Readers curious about unconventional cosmologies and life after death
core_themes: The origin, structure, and nature of the universe
The life and teachings of Jesus (referred to as Michael of Nebadon)
Humanity's relationship with God (the Universal Father)
Spiritual growth and the path of personal salvation
The organization and evolution of worlds and life
The purpose and destiny of human beings in the cosmic context
primary_purpose: To provide a comprehensive cosmological, theological, and philosophical framework uniting science, religion, and philosophy, and to reveal purported new truths about God, Jesus, and the universe for spiritual enlightenment and personal transformation.

structure_format.narrative_style: Formal, didactic, complex, and often academic or revelatory in tone
structure_format.organization: Divided into four parts: (1) The Central and Superuniverses, (2) The Local Universe, (3) The History of Urantia (Earth), (4) The Life and Teachings of Jesus
features: Extensive exposition with dense, sometimes technical language
Numbered papers and sections, totaling 196 papers
Purports to present revelatory information from non-human (celestial) authors

key_concepts_lessons: God (the Universal Father) is a personal, loving, and transcendent being intimately involved with creation.
The universe is vast, hierarchical, and inhabited by numerous orders of spiritual and material beings.
Human beings are evolving spiritually and destined for eternal life and adventure beyond earthly existence.
Jesus’ life, as revealed in The Urantia Book, is presented as a model for spiritual living and understanding of divine sonship.
Reconciliation of science, philosophy, and religion is possible through new, revelatory knowledge.
Spiritual progress occurs through personal relationship with God, service to others, and growth of the soul.
notable_features: Claims of celestial or revelatory authorship
Highly detailed cosmology, including descriptions of universe administration, planetary evolution, and the afterlife
Extensive reinterpretation and expansion of the life and teachings of Jesus (Part IV)
No official human author; production shrouded in mystery
cultural_historical_context: Published in mid-20th century America, a time marked by heightened interest in spiritual movements, metaphysical speculation, and attempts to reconcile science and religion. The Urantia Book emerged from a circle based in Chicago, allegedly through a process of 'revelation,' and has since inspired a small global movement.
reception_impact: Has inspired a dedicated community (the Urantia movement) and numerous study groups worldwide
Considered controversial and classified by most mainstream religions as a 'new religious text' or 'spiritual revelation,' sometimes as a cultic text
Praised by supporters for its depth, originality, and integrated approach to cosmology and spirituality
Criticized for anonymous authorship, unverifiable claims, and dense, difficult prose
Influenced some New Age, metaphysical, and alternative spiritual circles
